output.title: Black Friday commerce platform
output.description: An invented retailer, Larkspur Outfitters. A route table splits storefront traffic by path and rate-limits checkout; Checkout scales on CPU; an outbox feeds Kafka; KEDA wakes fulfilment on order lag; a bad deploy parks events in a DLQ while other consumer groups carry on.

contributors.label: Shoppers on the web, Larkspur app, Carrier scans
Shoppers on the web, Larkspur app, Carrier scans

annotations.text: In Live, each request route has its own colour and shape. The gateway caps checkout at 150 a second.
Outbox: the order and its event commit in one transaction. The relay publishes it; every consumer is idempotent.

simulations.title: Black Friday: doors open
simulations.description: Storefront traffic jumps five times in three seconds. The gateway caps checkout at 150 requests a second (429 for the rest), Checkout's HPA adds pods on CPU, and KEDA scales fulfilment on order lag.

action.text: A normal morning: 500 requests a second. The gateway's route table sends each path to its own service.
Doors open: 2,500 requests a second. The checkout route is capped at 150 a second; the rest get 429 and retry.
Checkout's CPU passes 70%, so its HPA starts more pods. Open its Live details for the replica history.
Orders reach Kafka through the outbox. Fulfilment lag rises and KEDA adds workers, up to the 24 partitions.
Traffic falls back. Lag drains, and every consumer group catches up without a dead letter.

simulations.title: A bad Loyalty deploy
simulations.description: Argo CD rolls out a Loyalty build that can't read a new order field. Its events fail three times and park in orders.dlq; the other consumer groups never notice. After the rollback, triage replays the parked events.

action.text: Five consumer groups read order events, each at its own pace and offset.
Argo CD rolls out Loyalty 4.2. It can't read the new gift-card field, so every order event fails.
After three tries each event parks in orders.dlq. Fulfilment, status and notifications carry on: their offsets are their own.
Rolled back. New events succeed again, and DLQ triage replays the parked ones into Loyalty.

expectations.label: Failed events park in the DLQ

simulations.title: The warehouse partner throttles
simulations.description: A sustained peak at the 3PL warehouse API, which allows 60 pick requests a second. KEDA keeps fulfilment lag low by adding workers, but every worker calls the same partner: the quota rejects the excess. Scaling consumers moved the bottleneck.

action.text: A sustained peak: about 130 orders a second reach Kafka.
KEDA adds fulfilment workers to keep lag near its target of 20 per worker.
Every worker calls the 3PL API, which allows 60 picks a second, so the rest are rejected. More workers can't raise a partner's quota: batch picks, or agree a higher limit.

expectations.label: The 3PL rejects picks over its quota
Fulfilment still keeps up with Kafka
